children: South Korea plans to merge its five state-run power generators into a single corporation and combine its national oil and gas companies, part of a broader overhaul of public institutions aimed at accelerating the energy transition and improving efficiency.
The government said in a statement on Thursday that it would consolidate five power generation companies into one entity to drive an energy transition centred on renewable energy.
The government considered that the current structure has led to overlapping investment and insufficient economies of scale, Yonhap News Agency reported.

The location of the merged company's headquarters has yet to be determined. Second Vice Finance Minister Huh Chang said the matter remained under discussion because the government had announced only the broad direction of the reform and would need to conduct further discussions, including with parliament and labour unions.
The government also plans to merge state-run Korea National Oil Corp (KNOC) and Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS).

This would help better respond to supply chain disruptions and geopolitical risks, formulate a more integrated national strategy for oil and gas, and increase South Korea's negotiating leverage with oil-producing countries and global energy companies, Yonhap said.
Huh said the government was aware of concerns stemming from differences in KNOC and KOGAS' financial structures and would pursue the merger in a way that maximised synergies.

The government also said it would restructure 109 public institutions overall through measures including strategic reorganisation, consolidation of overlapping functions and mergers of smaller bodies.
